text:
emily - AE: Quick thread — customer (FinisHealth) wants to run a week-long LLM POC in our Private offering. They have on‑prem inference hosts and want low-latency access. Need recommended connectivity: shared transit hub vs interface endpoints. Also will they accept our pricing estimate?

jordan - solutions eng: Short answer: both can work. Transit (TGW/shared services) gives a single egress point and easier source-IP preservation, but more infra for them. Interface endpoints (PrivateLink) are simpler for isolation and per-VPC access control, but can add per-GB and endpoint hour costs.

raj - netops: Notes from infra: if they use TGW/transit, we need to handshake BGP or static routes. Typical firewall rules: allow outbound TCP 443 to our egress IPs and UDP 123 for NTP. If they're using an on‑prem proxy, preserve-src-ip can be tricky — NAT in their edge will overwrite.

olivia - security: For the security questionnaire — we can confirm SOC2, TLS 1.2+ in transit, customer-managed KMS for Private, and audit logs retained X days (specify per contract). Also call out that Private deployments can be configured without internet egress if needed.

emily - AE: Customer asked about SNI/TLS inspect: their security team does TLS inspection and wants to terminate TLS for DLP. Will PrivateLink break anything?

jordan - solutions eng: If they TLS‑inspect at edge, SNI is visible pre‑inspect only if mTLS or client certs not used. With PrivateLink, our endpoint is an interface in their VPC — TLS stays end‑to‑end to our connector IPs. If their FW rewrites SNI or terminates TLS, source cert chains won't reach us → breaks mutual TLS. Recommend a passthrough policy for Redwood IPs.

raj - netops: Firewall sample snippet they can paste: 
```
# allow outbound to redwood private endpoints / egress
- proto: tcp
  ports: [443]
  dest_fqdn: ["connect.redwood.ai", "api.redwood-internal.example"]
  description: "Allow Private deploy traffic to Redwood"
```
And NAT note: if they need preserve-client-ip we require 1:1 NAT or no SNAT on the path to the interface endpoint.

emily - AE: Pricing question — they asked about hourly interface endpoint fees vs cross‑AZ data transfer. Jordan, any ballpark numbers to share for POC?

jordan - solutions eng: Ballpark (region-dependent): interface endpoint ~ $0.01–0.02/hr + data processing $0.01/GB (AWS-like). Transit/GW architecture => less endpoint fees but more inter-AZ data transfer and egress NAT costs. For a POC with <5TB/month, endpoints are often cheaper and faster to stand up. For steady >20TB, consider dedicated transit. Callout: Dedicated GPU capacity pricing separate (monthly commit or burst pricing) — sales should confirm their expected token throughput.

olivia - security: Add SCIM/SSO integration and IP allowlist steps to the questionnaire response. For private deployment: we can provide network diagrams and a shared statement of controls for legal.

raj - netops: One more operational risk: if they run deep TLS inspect with rewriting, session affinity breaks for streaming responses. If their app expects server-sent streaming, suggest marking Redwood endpoints as passthrough.

emily - AE: Action items: 1) raj — send a tiny firewall snippet + exact egress IP block list (for POC) 2) jordan — attach a short cost comparison table for endpoints vs transit for up to 10TB 3) olivia — draft answers for the security questionnaire bullets (SOC2, KMS, audit retention). Can we aim to have artifacts by EOD PST? :hourglass_flowing_sand:

deploy-bot: New deployment request created: DPL-7841 (private-poc-fin). Link: https://releases.redwood.ai/DPL-7841

raj - netops: I'll upload the egress IP list and the firewall snippet into the ticket by 1600 PST. Will include NAT/SNAT examples.

jordan - solutions eng: I'll mock a 3-row cost table and attach in the ticket — keeping numbers conservative.

olivia - security: Drafted questionnaire answers will be in the ticket too. If legal needs more, loop me in.

emily - AE: Thanks all — I'll update the customer after we attach the docs. :thumbsup:
